description:
Two in-process compiles of the SAME root publish BackendPrograms that differ
only in raw `Ty` numbering. Proven by decomposing the 1.5MB assertion diff into
per-kind id multisets:

    Ty            DIFFERS, symmetric diff size 448
    ValueId       identical multiset
    ShapeId       identical multiset
    FunctionId    identical multiset
    ExecutableKey identical multiset

Structure is identical; only the interner's first-intern order moved. This is
the exact class fz-k22.23/.28 chased (an unaudited unordered fold minting types
in different relative order), one fold further along.

## Repro

    cargo test --lib compiler2::product_drive_test::compiling_the_same_root_twice_publishes_byte_identical_backend_programs

The fixture is `fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz` (NOT
enum_take_drop_split -- fz-f98.18 lumped this red into that family and it is a
distinct root cause; the other three reds in that batch cleared with f98.18 and
this one did not move).

## Where to look

fz-k22.28 pinned the folds it found by sorting them:
`jobs/runtime_demand.rs`'s per-cone member list and per-value callable-flow
list (`HashMap` folds sorted by `ValueId`/`ExecutableKey`), and
`World::demand_activation_frontier_analyses`'s `HashSet<ActivationKey>` frontier
sorted by `StableSortKey`. Find the fold this fixture reaches that is NOT yet
pinned. Note [[feedback_sorting_is_a_barrier]]: a sort added here is a
determinism pin at a packaging point, which is the legitimate case -- but prefer
an ordered container at the source where one is available.

## Checks

- The test passes twice in a row from a clean build.
- The fold that moved is named, and either replaced with an ordered container or
  pinned with a comment saying which invariant the sort is standing in for.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better (currently lib 1448/1 with this as the
  only red; matrix 416/0).

comments.text:
INVESTIGATED. Mechanism identified and localized; three candidate folds probed,
one CONFIRMED as a contributor, two falsified as sufficient. Method below so it
can be redone.

## The symptom is arena ORDER, not content

Dumped the interner arena (id -> display, first-intern order) after each of the
two compiles, in one process. Both are 836 entries and mint the SAME types. They
first disagree at id 464, where two independent GROUPS swap places:

    A[464] alpha5056                                    B[464] ([int], :none, <2-brand union>) -> r0
    A[465] alpha5119                                    B[465] ([int], :none, (a2_p0,a2_p1)->a2_r | ...) -> r0
    A[466] (alpha5056) -> alpha5119#79closure[]         B[466] alpha5056
    A[467] ([int], :none, <2-brand union>) -> r0        B[467] alpha5119
    A[468] ([int], :none, ...) -> r0                    B[468] (alpha5056) -> alpha5119#79closure[]

The fresh-variable NUMBERS (5056, 5119) are identical in both runs, so variable
minting is deterministic. Only arena insertion order moved.

## It is job wake ORDER

Backtraced the mint of id 464 in each run: both are
`jobs::semantic::analyze_activation`, different activations. Logged every
`Scheduler::pop`. Both compiles pop exactly 1946 jobs and agree for 612 of them,
then swap a pair:

    step 613  A: AnalyzeActivation(FunctionId(204), Ty(105))
              B: AnalyzeActivation(FunctionId(193), Ty(145))
    step 614  A: AnalyzeActivation(FunctionId(193), Ty(145))
              B: AnalyzeActivation(FunctionId(204), Ty(105))

The agenda itself is a FIFO `VecDeque`, and `JobSet` (deps.rs) is already
insertion-ordered, so neither is the source.

## The source is the pending_changes drain order

Logged every `enqueue_dependents` wake with the fact that caused it. The two
compiles agree for 161 wakes, then wake the SAME job from two different facts in
opposite order:

    A[162] AnalyzeActivation(203, Ty83) via Current(ActivationInputs(203, Ty83))
    A[163] AnalyzeActivation(203, Ty83) via Current(ReturnType(204, Ty105))
    B[162] AnalyzeActivation(203, Ty83) via Current(ReturnType(204, Ty105))
    B[163] AnalyzeActivation(203, Ty83) via Current(ActivationInputs(203, Ty83))

Those two facts are both sitting in `Scheduler::complete`'s `pending_changes`
(scheduler.rs:302-363), which is drained LIFO. Whichever change is popped first
wakes its dependents first. So the question is what order `pending_changes` is
built in -- and it is fed by several HashSet folds.

## CONFIRMED contributor

`FactTable::mark_dirty` (facts.rs:333) iterates `output_keys: &HashSet<F>` to
build its `Vec<FactChange>`, and `enqueue_dependents` does
`pending_changes.extend(dirtied)` with it. Ordering that loop (temporary
`sort_by_key(format!("{k:?}"))`) MOVES the first wake divergence from 162 to
119 and changes its character:

    A: AnalyzeActivation(93, Ty65) via Current(ModuleDefined(ModuleId(9)))
    B: AnalyzeActivation(93, Ty65) via Current(ProtocolDispatch(ModuleId(2)))

Moves but does not remove. That is the signature of an audit, not a point fix:
each pinned fold exposes the next.

## FALSIFIED as sufficient (do not stop at these)

- `FactTable::extend_outputs` (facts.rs:302) iterates `output_keys: HashSet<F>`
  when the job handed it an ORDERED `Vec<F>`. Iterating the Vec instead: test
  still red, divergence still at step 613.
- `FactTable::replace_outputs` (facts.rs:240) iterates `touched: HashSet<F>`.
  Rebuilding `touched` as outputs-in-order then previous-only-keys: still red,
  still 613.
- Both of the above together with the mark_dirty ordering: still red.

Each is a genuine unordered fold and each should be fixed; none is the whole bug.

## The structural cause, and the shape of the fix

A job emits its outputs as an ORDERED `Vec<F>` (`Completion.outputs`). That
order is destroyed immediately and never recovered:

    facts.replace_outputs(..., outputs: Vec<F>)  -> builds HashSet<F>
    deps.replace_outputs(job, next_outputs: HashSet<F>)
    deps.outputs: HashMap<J, HashSet<F>>          <- stored unordered
    deps.output_keys(&job) -> HashSet<F>          <- handed to mark_dirty
    mark_dirty iterates it                        -> pending_changes order

Prefer preserving the job's own emission order end to end over sorting
([[feedback_sorting_is_a_barrier]] -- a sort here would be a determinism pin at
a packaging point, legitimate but second-best). compiler2 already has the idiom
twice: `JobSet` (deps.rs:22) and `Agenda` both pair an `order: Vec` with a
membership `HashSet`. Applying it to `DependencyIndex::outputs` makes
`output_keys` ordered by construction and `mark_dirty` deterministic without a
comparator.

## Repro harness used

1. Temporary `Types::probe_arena_dump()` returning `(0..arena.len()).map(|i|
   format!("{i}\t{}", display(Ty(i))))`.
2. A temporary test compiling the fixture twice in ONE process and diffing the
   two dumps for the first divergent id.
3. `PROBE_TY=<id>` env check inside `TypeInterner::intern` printing
   `Backtrace::force_capture()` when `arena.len()` matches.
4. `PROBE_JOBS=1` in `Scheduler::pop` and `PROBE_ENQ=1` in `enqueue_dependents`
   (printing job AND fact_use), then diffing the two halves of the log.

Two compiles in one process is what exposes this: Rust's `RandomState` differs
per HashMap instance, so the second compile's maps iterate differently from the
first's.

title: Ty interner numbering is nondeterministic across two in-process compiles of enum_predicate_search
